question: How many tonnes of pizza do people in Chicago eat on an average day in 2026?

target.what: Total mass of pizza consumed by people in Chicago (city of Chicago, all pizza types, all consumption occasions: restaurant, takeout, delivery, and home-prepared from purchased/frozen pizza) on an average day in calendar year 2026
target.cadence: Annual average daily flow, not published
target.caveats: Ambiguity: 'Chicago' taken as the city of Chicago (approx. 2.7M residents), not the Chicago metropolitan area (approx. 9.5M) or Chicagoland CSA; alternative metro interpretation would scale the answer by roughly 3-3.5x. 'People in Chicago' includes residents plus visitors/tourists and commuters eati

candidates.perspective: National/industry pizza market data provider or trade association
candidates.hypothesis: US per-capita pizza consumption (kg/person/year) multiplied by Chicago population gives a first-order total; Chicago's pizza culture and dense restaurant supply likely push it above the national average, so a Chicago adjustment factor (restaurant density or sales-per-capita ratio) is needed. Target = per_capita_pizza_kg * population / 365.
candidates.data_to_find: US annual pizza consumption or pizza sales volume in tonnes (or sales USD with average price per pizza to convert), latest pre-cutoff year; US population; Chicago city population estimate for 2025/2026 from Census Bureau. Substitute: national pizza sales USD from industry reports divided by average price per pizza and average pizza mass.
search_hints: US pizza consumption per capita annual statistics
pizza industry sales volume tons United States 2024
how much pizza does the average American eat per year

candidates.hypothesis: Chicago food-away-from-home and pizza-restaurant sales (USD) divided by average price per pizza and average pizza mass yields pizza mass sold; pizza's share of Chicago restaurant sales times total Chicago restaurant sales gives pizza sales. Target = (Chicago restaurant sales * pizza share) / price_per_pizza * mass_per_pizza / 365.
candidates.data_to_find: Chicago metro or city restaurant/food-service sales totals (pre-cutoff, e.g. 2023-2025); pizza's share of limited-service/restaurant sales; average pizza price and average pizza weight (grams) in US. Substitute: number of pizza establishments times average daily sales per establishment.

candidates.perspective: Pizza restaurant operators and delivery platforms in Chicago
candidates.hypothesis: Number of pizza-serving establishments in Chicago times average pizzas sold per establishment per day times average pizza mass gives total pizza throughput. Target = establishments * pizzas_per_day * mass_per_pizza.
candidates.data_to_find: Count of pizza restaurants/pizzerias in Chicago (city or metro) from business listings, health inspections, or industry counts; average daily pizza sales per pizzeria (chain benchmarks or POS data); average pizza mass. Substitute: chain store counts (Domino's, Pizza Hut, local chains) plus independent estimate.

candidates.hypothesis: 2026 pizza mass depends on Chicago population trend, visitor volume, and pizza price inflation (which may suppress volume). Adjusting a 2024/2025 baseline by population growth, tourism recovery, and real price change projects 2026. Target_2026 = baseline_mass * (1 + pop_growth) * (1 + visitor_effect) * (1 + price_volume_elasticity * real_price_change).

assessment.note: Same rentechdigital listing count of 1,987 Chicago pizza restaurants as of 2026-04-01, repeated across directions; one underlying measurement, not four independent confirmations.
Single-owner count 914 = 46% of 1,987; same source, internally consistent, one measurement.
Brand-affiliated count 1,073 = 54% of 1,987; same source, complements the single-owner split.
Website presence split 1,848/139; same listing database, adds no independent information about pizza volume.
Social-media and phone presence counts from the same listing scrape; descriptive of the directory, not of throughput.
Average restaurant age ~10 years 2 months, repeated; same source.
USDA/WWEIA NHANES 2017-March 2020: 11-12% of the US population eats pizza on any given day; the two figures are the same survey with slightly different age framing.
Meal-occasion and snack shares of pizza intake from the same NHANES analysis; consistent internal breakdown.
Source-of-pizza shares (restaurant 56%, grocery 26%, school 12%, other 6%) from the same NHANES analysis; sums to 100%.

US per-capita cheese series from USDA ERS-derived reporting; 2024 total 48 lb, natural 39.9 lb, mozzarella 12.5 lb. Different vintages (cheesemarketnews vs newsbreak) but same underlying ERS data; treat as one cheese-availability signal.
Choose Chicago 2025 tourism metrics; 56.8M visitors, 11.9M room nights, 69.1% occupancy. Same source family, mutually consistent; useful for visitor exposure but not for pizza mass directly.
USDA ERS CPI series: food-away-from-home +3.4% y/y Aug 2026, +3.8% 2025, +4.1% 2024; all-food +2.7% Aug 2026. Consistent inflation context for a price/volume adjustment.
1986 survey: Chicago 34.8 pizza meals/person/year vs LA <20; supports a Chicago pizza-culture premium over national norms, but is 40 years old and measures meals not mass.

Chicago pizzeria operating statistics (2011-2014): Ranalli's ~1,200-1,500 pizzas/week, Dimo's 29,760 slices/month, Bar Toma ingredient flows. Same Eater Chicago feature; useful for per-establishment throughput and ingredient mass fractions, but old and small-sample.

methods.rationale: Per-capita exposure route (d1/d4): Chicago residents x daily pizza-eater share x culture multiplier x serving mass. methods.rationale: Physical-flow cross-check (d5): national mozzarella disappearance per capita (p54) x Chicago population gives a cheese-flow scale. This is NOT a pizza-mass estimate on its own — mozzarella is used in lasagna and other foods, and pizza mass is several times cheese mass — so it is declared a part/reference method and never averaged with full estimates. It is retained only to sanity-check the order of magnitude of cheese embedded in the m1/m2 results.

assumptions.name: Chicago pizza-culture multiplier on national per-capita pizza intake
assumptions.rationale: The 1986 survey (p120, p121) put Chicago at 34.8 pizza meals/person/year vs LA under 20, roughly 1.7-1.8x a comparable large city, and Chicago's dense pizza-restaurant supply (p19) supports above-national intake. National NHANES intake (p34) is the base; a 1.3x central multiplier with a wide range reflects that the 1986 gap is old and measures meals, not mass, and that national pizza culture has converged since.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to scale US per-capita pizza intake (p34) to Chicago residents; not applied to visitor exposure.
assumptions.falsified_by: A recent Chicago-specific per-capita pizza consumption figure showing Chicago at or below the national average.

assumptions.name: Average pizza mass consumed per eating occasion
assumptions.rationale: A pizza-eating occasion is typically 2-3 slices of a ~100-120 g slice, or a personal pizza; 250 g central with a 150-400 g range spans a light snack occasion to a deep-dish meal. No kept point gives a direct average serving mass, so this is an explicit modelling assumption grounded in typical slice weights.
assumptions.applies_when: Multiplied by the share of people eating pizza on a given day (p34) to get daily per-capita pizza mass.
assumptions.falsified_by: A sourced average pizza serving weight for US or Chicago eaters materially outside 150-400 g.

assumptions.name: Chicago city population, 2026
assumptions.rationale: Pinned target is the city of Chicago (~2.7M residents per recent Census estimates), not the 9.5M MSA. Range reflects Census-estimate uncertainty and modest recent decline.
assumptions.applies_when: Resident base for the per-capita route; excludes visitors and commuters, which are handled separately or noted as a small upward bias.
assumptions.falsified_by: A 2026 Census population estimate for the city of Chicago outside 2.55-2.85M.

assumptions.name: Average whole-pizza mass sold per Chicago pizzeria
assumptions.rationale: Chicago thin-crust pizzas run ~700-900 g, deep-dish/stuffed ~1.2-1.8 kg; a sales-weighted mix centers near 900 g. Used only in the establishment-throughput route where pizza counts are converted to mass.
assumptions.applies_when: Multiplied by pizzas sold per establishment per day in the d3 route.
assumptions.falsified_by: Sourced average Chicago pizza weight outside 600-1400 g.

assumptions.name: Average pizzas sold per Chicago pizzeria per day

The 1,987-location directory (p19) surely includes low-volume and non-pizza-primary venues, so the citywide average is far below a flagship. 45/day central with 20-90 range reflects that mix.
assumptions.applies_when: Multiplied by the 1,987 listed pizza establishments (p19) to get daily pizza count in the d3 route.
assumptions.falsified_by: A recent survey of Chicago pizzeria average daily volume outside 20-90 pizzas.

p120.role: 1986 Chicago per-capita pizza meals per year, adjusted to 2026 by a3

a2.role: average pizza mass per pizza meal

a3.role: Chicago pizza-culture adjustment to the 1986 meal rate

methods.rationale: Per-capita pizza-meal route anchored on the 1986 Chicago survey (p120), converted to mass via an assumed per-meal mass and adjusted for four decades of change and non-resident eating. Largest uncertainty is the 1986-to-2026 transfer and the per-meal mass; the survey's 'pizza meal' definition is undefined.

p34.role: national share of population consuming pizza on any given day, transferred to Chicago by a4

a4.role: Chicago adjustment to national daily pizza-eater share

a5.role: average servings per pizza eater per day

methods.rationale: Base-rate route: national NHANES daily pizza-eater share (p34) times Chicago population, adjusted for Chicago culture, servings per eater, and serving mass. Depends on a national-to-Chicago transfer and on assumed serving mass; the NHANES data are pre-2020.

p19.role: count of pizza restaurants in Chicago, April 2026

a7.role: average pizzas sold per Chicago pizzeria per day

a9.role: share of Chicago pizza mass from non-establishment sources

methods.rationale: Capacity/throughput route: 1,987 Chicago pizza establishments (p19) times assumed per-store daily pizza volume and whole-pizza mass, grossed up for home/frozen/retail pizza. The establishment count is a listing count, not a throughput measure; per-store volume and pizza mass are the dominant uncertainties.

a10.role: Chicago share of US pizza-segment sales

a11.role: average price per kg of pizza

methods.rationale: Spend-based route: national pizza-segment sales (p150, a forecast) allocated to Chicago by an assumed population-based share, converted to mass via an assumed price per kg. Depends on a forecast, a Chicago allocation, and a price conversion; weakest of the routes but structurally independent of the per-capita and establishment routes.

assumptions.name: Chicago city population, 2026
assumptions.rationale: City of Chicago population is roughly 2.7M in recent Census estimates; no kept point supplies it, so it is assumed with a modest range reflecting migration uncertainty.
assumptions.applies_when: Target is the city of Chicago, not the metro area.
assumptions.falsified_by: A Census 2026 city population estimate outside the range.

assumptions.name: Average pizza mass per pizza meal
assumptions.rationale: A pizza meal is typically 2-3 slices of a ~2.5-3 kg whole pizza or a personal pizza; 0.35 kg is central with a wide range covering thin-crust slices and deep-dish portions. No kept point gives a direct per-meal mass.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to convert pizza-meal counts to mass.
assumptions.falsified_by: A sourced average slice or whole-pizza weight implying a materially different per-meal mass.

assumptions.name: Chicago pizza-culture adjustment to the 1986 meal rate
assumptions.rationale: The 1986 survey already ranked Chicago highest; the adjustment covers four decades of change in eating patterns and whether the 1986 rate still holds. Centered at 1 with a wide range.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to transfer the 1986 Chicago pizza-meal rate to 2026.
assumptions.falsified_by: Modern Chicago-specific pizza-frequency survey data showing a materially different rate.

assumptions.name: Chicago adjustment to national daily pizza-eater share
assumptions.rationale: Chicago's dense pizza culture and restaurant supply suggest a modestly above-national daily eater share; centered slightly above 1 with a wide range.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to transfer the national NHANES daily pizza-eater share to Chicago.
assumptions.falsified_by: Chicago-specific consumption-frequency data near or below the national average.

assumptions.name: Average servings per pizza eater per day
assumptions.rationale: Most pizza eaters have one pizza occasion per day, some have two; 1.3 is a central value with a range.
assumptions.applies_when: Used with the daily eater share to get daily servings per capita.
assumptions.falsified_by: Dietary-recall data showing a materially different servings-per-eater rate.

assumptions.name: Average pizza serving mass
assumptions.rationale: A serving is roughly one to two slices; 0.15 kg is a central value with a wide range.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to convert daily servings to mass.
assumptions.falsified_by: A sourced average slice weight implying a materially different serving mass.

assumptions.name: Average pizzas sold per Chicago pizzeria per day
assumptions.rationale: The 2014 Eater figures (p130, p132) imply roughly 160-215 pizzas/week at two busy establishments (~25-30/day); a citywide average across 1,987 listings including low-volume venues is plausibly higher in count but lower per store; 60/day is central with a wide range.
assumptions.applies_when: Used with the establishment count to estimate daily pizza throughput.
assumptions.falsified_by: A current Chicago per-pizzeria volume survey outside the range.

assumptions.name: Average whole-pizza mass
assumptions.rationale: Chicago thin, deep-dish, and stuffed pizzas vary widely; 1.0 kg is a central whole-pizza mass with a wide range.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to convert pizza counts to mass.
assumptions.falsified_by: A sourced average Chicago pizza weight outside the range.

assumptions.name: Share of Chicago pizza mass from non-establishment (home/frozen/retail) sources
assumptions.rationale: Technomic reports 14% of pizza spend is retail (p145); mass share is likely somewhat higher because retail pizza is cheaper per kg; 0.2 is central.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to gross up establishment throughput to all pizza consumption.
assumptions.falsified_by: Chicago-specific data showing a materially different retail/home share.

assumptions.name: Chicago share of US pizza-segment sales
assumptions.rationale: Chicago city population is ~0.8% of the US; pizza culture may push its share slightly above population share; 0.008 is central.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to allocate national pizza-segment sales to Chicago.
assumptions.falsified_by: Chicago-specific pizza-sales data implying a materially different share.

assumptions.name: Average price per kg of pizza
assumptions.rationale: Pizza prices per kg vary by type and channel; $12/kg is central and consistent with typical per-pizza prices and masses.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to convert pizza spend to mass.
assumptions.falsified_by: Sourced average pizza price per kg outside the range.

assumptions.name: Visitor/commuter exposure adjustment to resident pizza mass
assumptions.rationale: Chicago has substantial visitors and commuters (p93, p95) who eat pizza in the city; a modest uplift over resident-only mass is plausible.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to adjust resident-based estimates for non-resident eating in Chicago.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that visitors/commuters contribute negligibly or substantially more.

p120.role: 1986 Chicago per-capita pizza meals per year, adjusted to 2026 by a3

a2.role: average pizza mass per pizza meal

a3.role: Chicago pizza-culture adjustment to the 1986 meal rate

previous_methods.rationale: Per-capita pizza-meal route anchored on the 1986 Chicago survey (p120), converted to mass via an assumed per-meal mass and adjusted for four decades of change and non-resident eating. Largest uncertainty is the 1986-to-2026 transfer and the per-meal mass; the survey's 'pizza meal' definition is undefined.

p34.role: national share of population consuming pizza on any given day, transferred to Chicago by a4

a4.role: Chicago adjustment to national daily pizza-eater share

a5.role: average servings per pizza eater per day

previous_methods.rationale: Base-rate route: national NHANES daily pizza-eater share (p34) times Chicago population, adjusted for Chicago culture, servings per eater, and serving mass. Depends on a national-to-Chicago transfer and on assumed serving mass; the NHANES data are pre-2020.

p19.role: count of pizza restaurants in Chicago, April 2026

a7.role: average pizzas sold per Chicago pizzeria per day

a9.role: share of Chicago pizza mass from non-establishment sources

previous_methods.rationale: Capacity/throughput route: 1,987 Chicago pizza establishments (p19) times assumed per-store daily pizza volume and whole-pizza mass, grossed up for home/frozen/retail pizza. The establishment count is a listing count, not a throughput measure; per-store volume and pizza mass are the dominant uncertainties.

p150.role: expected US pizza-segment sales this year, allocated to Chicago by a10

a10.role: Chicago share of US pizza-segment sales

a11.role: average price per kg of pizza

previous_methods.rationale: Spend-based route: national pizza-segment sales (p150, a forecast) allocated to Chicago by an assumed population-based share, converted to mass via an assumed price per kg. Depends on a forecast, a Chicago allocation, and a price conversion; weakest of the routes but structurally independent of the per-capita and establishment routes.

previous_assumptions.name: Chicago city population, 2026
previous_assumptions.rationale: City of Chicago population is roughly 2.7M (Census estimates in the 2020s); no kept point supplies it, so it is assumed with a modest range reflecting recent estimates and migration uncertainty.
previous_assumptions.applies_when: Target is interpreted as the city of Chicago, not the metro area.
previous_assumptions.falsified_by: A Census 2026 city population estimate outside the range.

previous_assumptions.name: Average pizza mass per pizza meal
previous_assumptions.rationale: A pizza meal is typically 2-3 slices of a ~2.5-3 kg whole pizza, or a personal pizza; 0.35 kg is a central value with a wide range covering thin-crust slices and deep-dish portions. No kept point gives a direct per-meal mass.
previous_assumptions.applies_when: Used to convert pizza-meal counts to mass.
previous_assumptions.falsified_by: A sourced average slice or whole-pizza weight implying a materially different per-meal mass.

previous_assumptions.name: Chicago pizza-culture adjustment to the 1986 meal rate
previous_assumptions.rationale: The 1986 survey already ranked Chicago highest; the adjustment accounts for four decades of change in eating patterns and for whether the 1986 rate still holds. Centered at 1 with a wide range.
previous_assumptions.applies_when: Used to transfer the 1986 Chicago pizza-meal rate to 2026.
previous_assumptions.falsified_by: Modern Chicago-specific pizza-frequency survey data showing a materially different rate.

previous_assumptions.name: Chicago adjustment to national daily pizza-eater share
previous_assumptions.rationale: Chicago's dense pizza culture and restaurant supply suggest a modestly above-national daily eater share; centered slightly above 1 with a wide range.
previous_assumptions.applies_when: Used to transfer the national NHANES daily pizza-eater share to Chicago.
previous_assumptions.falsified_by: Chicago-specific consumption-frequency data near or below the national average.

previous_assumptions.name: Average servings per pizza eater per day
previous_assumptions.rationale: Most pizza eaters have one pizza occasion per day, some have two; 1.3 is a central value with a range.
previous_assumptions.applies_when: Used with the daily eater share to get daily servings per capita.
previous_assumptions.falsified_by: Dietary-recall data showing a materially different servings-per-eater rate.

previous_assumptions.name: Average pizza serving mass
previous_assumptions.rationale: A serving is roughly one to two slices; 0.15 kg is a central value with a wide range.
previous_assumptions.applies_when: Used to convert daily servings to mass.
previous_assumptions.falsified_by: A sourced average slice weight implying a materially different serving mass.

previous_assumptions.name: Average pizzas sold per Chicago pizzeria per day
previous_assumptions.rationale: The 2014 Eater figures (p130, p132) imply roughly 160-215 pizzas/week at two busy establishments, i.e. ~25-30/day; a citywide average across 1,987 listings including low-volume venues is plausibly higher in count but lower per store; 60/day is a central value with a wide range.
previous_assumptions.applies_when: Used with the establishment count to estimate daily pizza throughput.
previous_assumptions.falsified_by: A current Chicago per-pizzeria volume survey outside the range.

previous_assumptions.name: Average whole-pizza mass
previous_assumptions.rationale: Chicago thin, deep-dish, and stuffed pizzas vary widely; 1.0 kg is a central whole-pizza mass with a wide range.
previous_assumptions.applies_when: Used to convert pizza counts to mass.
previous_assumptions.falsified_by: A sourced average Chicago pizza weight outside the range.

previous_assumptions.name: Share of Chicago pizza mass from non-establishment (home/frozen/retail) sources
previous_assumptions.rationale: Technomic reports 14% of pizza spend is retail (p145); mass share is likely somewhat higher because retail pizza is cheaper per kg; 0.2 is a central value.
previous_assumptions.applies_when: Used to gross up establishment throughput to all pizza consumption.
previous_assumptions.falsified_by: Chicago-specific data showing a materially different retail/home share.

previous_assumptions.name: Chicago share of US pizza-segment sales
previous_assumptions.rationale: Chicago city population is ~0.8% of the US; pizza culture may push its share slightly above population share; 0.008 is a central value.
previous_assumptions.applies_when: Used to allocate national pizza-segment sales to Chicago.
previous_assumptions.falsified_by: Chicago-specific pizza-sales data implying a materially different share.

previous_assumptions.name: Average price per kg of pizza
previous_assumptions.rationale: Pizza prices per kg vary by type and channel; $12/kg is a central value consistent with typical per-pizza prices and masses.
previous_assumptions.applies_when: Used to convert pizza spend to mass.
previous_assumptions.falsified_by: Sourced average pizza price per kg outside the range.

previous_assumptions.name: Visitor/commuter exposure adjustment to resident pizza mass
previous_assumptions.rationale: Chicago has substantial visitors and commuters (p93, p95) who eat pizza in the city; a modest uplift over resident-only mass is plausible.
previous_assumptions.applies_when: Used to adjust resident-based estimates for non-resident eating in Chicago.
previous_assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that visitors/commuters contribute negligibly or substantially more.

methods.label: m1

params.formula: p120 * a1 * a2 * a3 * a12 / k_days_per_year

p120.role: 1986 Chicago per-capita pizza meals per year, adjusted to 2026 by a3

a2.role: average pizza mass per pizza meal

a3.role: Chicago pizza-culture adjustment to the 1986 meal rate

methods.rationale: Per-capita pizza-meal route anchored on the 1986 Chicago survey (p120), converted to mass via an assumed per-meal mass and adjusted for four decades of change and non-resident eating. Largest uncertainty is the 1986-to-2026 transfer and the per-meal mass; the survey's 'pizza meal' definition is undefined.

inputs_detail.name: p120
inputs_detail.unit: pizza meals per person per year

methods.label: m2

p34.role: national share of population consuming pizza on any given day, transferred to Chicago by a4

a4.role: Chicago adjustment to national daily pizza-eater share

a5.role: average servings per pizza eater per day

methods.rationale: Base-rate route: national NHANES daily pizza-eater share (p34) times Chicago population, adjusted for Chicago culture, servings per eater, and serving mass. Depends on a national-to-Chicago transfer and on assumed serving mass; the NHANES data are pre-2020.

methods.label: m3

p19.role: count of pizza restaurants in Chicago, April 2026

a7.role: average pizzas sold per Chicago pizzeria per day

a9.role: share of Chicago pizza mass from non-establishment sources

methods.rationale: Capacity/throughput route: 1,987 Chicago pizza establishments (p19) times assumed per-store daily pizza volume and whole-pizza mass, grossed up for home/frozen/retail pizza. The establishment count is a listing count, not a throughput measure; per-store volume and pizza mass are the dominant uncertainties.

methods.label: m4

p150.role: expected US pizza-segment sales this year, allocated to Chicago by a10

a10.role: Chicago share of US pizza-segment sales

a11.role: average price per kg of pizza

methods.rationale: Spend-based route: national pizza-segment sales (p150, a forecast) allocated to Chicago by an assumed population-based share, converted to mass via an assumed price per kg. Depends on a forecast, a Chicago allocation, and a price conversion; weakest of the routes but structurally independent of the per-capita and establishment routes.

kept.name: Chicago city population, 2026
kept.rationale: City of Chicago population is roughly 2.7M in recent Census estimates; no kept point supplies it, so it is assumed with a modest range reflecting migration uncertainty.
kept.applies_when: Target is the city of Chicago, not the metro area.
kept.falsified_by: A Census 2026 city population estimate outside the range.

kept.name: Average pizza mass per pizza meal
kept.rationale: A pizza meal is typically 2-3 slices of a ~2.5-3 kg whole pizza or a personal pizza; 0.35 kg is central with a wide range covering thin-crust slices and deep-dish portions. No kept point gives a direct per-meal mass.
kept.applies_when: Used to convert pizza-meal counts to mass.
kept.falsified_by: A sourced average slice or whole-pizza weight implying a materially different per-meal mass.

kept.name: Chicago pizza-culture adjustment to the 1986 meal rate
kept.rationale: The 1986 survey already ranked Chicago highest; the adjustment covers four decades of change in eating patterns and whether the 1986 rate still holds. Centered at 1 with a wide range.
kept.applies_when: Used to transfer the 1986 Chicago pizza-meal rate to 2026.
kept.falsified_by: Modern Chicago-specific pizza-frequency survey data showing a materially different rate.

kept.name: Chicago adjustment to national daily pizza-eater share
kept.rationale: Chicago's dense pizza culture and restaurant supply suggest a modestly above-national daily eater share; centered slightly above 1 with a wide range.
kept.applies_when: Used to transfer the national NHANES daily pizza-eater share to Chicago.
kept.falsified_by: Chicago-specific consumption-frequency data near or below the national average.

kept.name: Average servings per pizza eater per day
kept.rationale: Most pizza eaters have one pizza occasion per day, some have two; 1.3 is a central value with a range.
kept.applies_when: Used with the daily eater share to get daily servings per capita.
kept.falsified_by: Dietary-recall data showing a materially different servings-per-eater rate.

kept.name: Average pizza serving mass
kept.rationale: A serving is roughly one to two slices; 0.15 kg is a central value with a wide range.
kept.applies_when: Used to convert daily servings to mass.
kept.falsified_by: A sourced average slice weight implying a materially different serving mass.

kept.name: Average pizzas sold per Chicago pizzeria per day
kept.rationale: The 2014 Eater figures (p130, p132) imply roughly 160-215 pizzas/week at two busy establishments (~25-30/day); a citywide average across 1,987 listings including low-volume venues is plausibly higher in count but lower per store; 60/day is central with a wide range.
kept.applies_when: Used with the establishment count to estimate daily pizza throughput.
kept.falsified_by: A current Chicago per-pizzeria volume survey outside the range.

kept.name: Average whole-pizza mass
kept.rationale: Chicago thin, deep-dish, and stuffed pizzas vary widely; 1.0 kg is a central whole-pizza mass with a wide range.
kept.applies_when: Used to convert pizza counts to mass.
kept.falsified_by: A sourced average Chicago pizza weight outside the range.

kept.name: Share of Chicago pizza mass from non-establishment (home/frozen/retail) sources
kept.rationale: Technomic reports 14% of pizza spend is retail (p145); mass share is likely somewhat higher because retail pizza is cheaper per kg; 0.2 is central.
kept.applies_when: Used to gross up establishment throughput to all pizza consumption.
kept.falsified_by: Chicago-specific data showing a materially different retail/home share.

kept.name: Chicago share of US pizza-segment sales
kept.rationale: Chicago city population is ~0.8% of the US; pizza culture may push its share slightly above population share; 0.008 is central.
kept.applies_when: Used to allocate national pizza-segment sales to Chicago.
kept.falsified_by: Chicago-specific pizza-sales data implying a materially different share.

kept.name: Average price per kg of pizza
kept.rationale: Pizza prices per kg vary by type and channel; $12/kg is central and consistent with typical per-pizza prices and masses.
kept.applies_when: Used to convert pizza spend to mass.
kept.falsified_by: Sourced average pizza price per kg outside the range.

kept.name: Visitor/commuter exposure adjustment to resident pizza mass
kept.rationale: Chicago has substantial visitors and commuters (p93, p95) who eat pizza in the city; a modest uplift over resident-only mass is plausible.
kept.applies_when: Used to adjust resident-based estimates for non-resident eating in Chicago.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that visitors/commuters contribute negligibly or substantially more.

The best estimate is 97.13 t/day (80% model-based interval 40.01 to 236 t/day) for total pizza mass consumed by people in the city of Chicago on an average day in calendar year 2026, covering restaurant, takeout, delivery, and home-prepared pizza.

Four routes were averaged with equal weights: a per-capita pizza-meal route anchored on 34.8 pizza meals per person per year from a [n] Chicago survey; a base-rate route using 11 percent of population from NHANES; a capacity route built on 1,987 pizza restaurants; and a spend route using 50,000,000,000 USD sales. Only these points are observed; population, per-meal and serving mass, per-store volume, whole-pizza mass, retail share, price per kg, and visitor adjustments are all analyst assumptions, and the [n] and national figures require transfers to Chicago in 2026.

The interval reflects input uncertainty only, not demonstrated accuracy. The biggest risk is the undefined [n] 'pizza meal' and its four-decade transfer, plus per-meal mass. Better evidence would be a current Chicago-specific pizza consumption or sales survey.

Key assumptions (proposed by the analyst model, not observed; code samples each one between the bounds shown):
- a1 Chicago city population, 2026: 2,700,000 people, range 1,907,878 to 3,815,757 (range widened by code); used by m1, m2. Overturned by: A Census 2026 city population estimate outside the range.
- a2 Average pizza mass per pizza meal: 0.35 kg per pizza meal, range 0.2 to 0.55; used by m1. Overturned by: A sourced average slice or whole-pizza weight implying a materially different per-meal mass.
- a3 Chicago pizza-culture adjustment to the [n] meal rate: 1 dimensionless, range 0.7 to 1.4; used by m1. Overturned by: Modern Chicago-specific pizza-frequency survey data showing a materially different rate.
- a4 Chicago adjustment to national daily pizza-eater share: 1.15 dimensionless, range 0.8216 to 1.643 (range widened by code); used by m2. Overturned by: Chicago-specific consumption-frequency data near or below the national average.
- a5 Average servings per pizza eater per day: 1.3 servings per eater per day, range 0.9487 to 1.897 (range widened by code); used by m2. Overturned by: Dietary-recall data showing a materially different servings-per-eater rate.
- a6 Average pizza serving mass: 0.15 kg per serving, range 0.1 to 0.25; used by m2. Overturned by: A sourced average slice weight implying a materially different serving mass.
- a7 Average pizzas sold per Chicago pizzeria per day: 60 pizzas per establishment per day, range 30 to 120; used by m3. Overturned by: A current Chicago per-pizzeria volume survey outside the range.
- a8 Average whole-pizza mass: 1 kg per pizza, range 0.6 to 1.6; used by m3. Overturned by: A sourced average Chicago pizza weight outside the range.
- a9 Share of Chicago pizza mass from non-establishment (home/frozen/retail) sources: 0.2 fraction, range 0.1 to 0.35; used by m3. Overturned by: Chicago-specific data showing a materially different retail/home share.
- a10 Chicago share of US pizza-segment sales: 0.008 fraction, range 0.005 to 0.012; used by m4. Overturned by: Chicago-specific pizza-sales data implying a materially different share.
- a11 Average price per kg of pizza: 12 USD per kg, range 8 to 18; used by m4. Overturned by: Sourced average pizza price per kg outside the range.
- a12 Visitor/commuter exposure adjustment to resident pizza mass: 1.05 dimensionless, range 0.7583 to 1.517 (range widened by code); used by m1, m2. Overturned by: Evidence that visitors/commuters contribute negligibly or substantially more.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
